prompt: In John, what does the opening of the Gospel call Jesus, who was with God in the beginning and became flesh?
explanation: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God; and the Word became flesh.

prompt: In John, what does Jesus offer the Samaritan woman at the well?
explanation: Whoever drinks the water Jesus gives will never be thirsty again; it becomes a spring welling up to eternal life.

prompt: In John, why do the Jewish leaders seek to kill Jesus after he heals the invalid at the pool of Bethesda?
options: He healed on the Sabbath and called God his own Father, making himself equal with God
He told the healed man to stop offering sacrifices at the temple
He claimed in front of the council to be greater than Moses
He publicly forgave the invalid's sins, which only the priests could do
explanation: John says they sought to kill him because he broke the Sabbath and called God his own Father.

prompt: In John, what does Jesus say the good shepherd does for the sheep, unlike the hired hand?
options: He lays down his life for the sheep
He leaves the ninety-nine to search for the one that strays
He separates the sheep from the goats at the judgment
He drives the wolf away with his staff and keeps watch all night
explanation: The hired hand flees when the wolf comes, but the good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep.

prompt: In John, how many days has Lazarus been in the tomb when Jesus arrives at Bethany?
explanation: Martha objects that there will be an odor, since Lazarus has been dead four days.

prompt: In John, what part of the disciples' bodies does Jesus wash at the Last Supper?
explanation: Jesus ties a towel around his waist and washes the disciples' feet, over Peter's objection.

prompt: In John, who strikes the high priest's servant and cuts off his ear when Jesus is arrested?
explanation: Simon Peter draws his sword and cuts off the right ear of the high priest's servant, Malchus.

prompt: In John, what does Thomas say when he sees the risen Jesus and his wounds?
options: "My Lord and my God!"
"Rabbi, you are the Son of God!"
"Lord, to whom shall we go?"
"Truly this was the Son of God!"
explanation: Thomas answers, "My Lord and my God!" and Jesus blesses those who have not seen and yet believe.

prompt: In John, what does John the Baptist call Jesus when he sees him coming toward him?
explanation: "Behold, the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world!"

prompt: In John, what does Nicodemus, who first came to Jesus by night, do after Jesus' death?
options: He brings myrrh and aloes and helps Joseph of Arimathea bury Jesus
He testifies against Jesus at the trial before Caiaphas
He is baptized by Jesus' disciples in the Jordan and leaves the Pharisees
He hides Jesus in his house during the Feast of Booths
explanation: Nicodemus brings about seventy-five pounds of myrrh and aloes for the burial.

prompt: In John, what question does the risen Jesus ask Peter three times by the Sea of Tiberias?
options: "Do you love me?"
"Will you deny me again?"
"Who do you say that I am?"
"Why did you doubt?"
explanation: Three times Jesus asks "Do you love me?" and three times tells Peter to feed his sheep, undoing the three denials.

prompt: In John, what does Judas object to when Mary anoints Jesus' feet with costly ointment at Bethany?
options: That the ointment was not sold and the money given to the poor
That a woman had touched a rabbi in public
That the ointment should have been kept for Jesus' burial
That Lazarus's family had wasted money owed to the treasury
explanation: Judas says it because he was a thief who helped himself to the money bag, not because he cared for the poor.

prompt: In John, what does Caiaphas argue when the council debates what to do about Jesus after Lazarus is raised?
options: It is better for one man to die for the people than for the whole nation to perish
Jesus should be handed to the Romans, since only they can carry out a death sentence
Jesus should be brought before the council to answer for calling himself the Son of God
Jesus should be arrested only after the Passover, to avoid a riot among the crowds
explanation: John notes that Caiaphas, being high priest that year, prophesied that Jesus would die for the nation.

prompt: In John, what does Pilate do after examining Jesus during the trial?
options: He finds no guilt in Jesus but still hands him over to be crucified
He sends Jesus to Herod, who mocks him and sends him back
He has Jesus scourged and then releases him with a warning
He condemns Jesus for refusing to pay tribute to Caesar
explanation: Three times Pilate says he finds no guilt in Jesus, then delivers him over when the crowd invokes Caesar.

prompt: In John, whom does the crowd ask Pilate to release instead of Jesus?
explanation: Pilate offers to release one prisoner at the Passover, and the crowd cries out for Barabbas, a robber.

prompt: In John, what does Thomas insist on before he will believe the other disciples' report that Jesus is alive?
options: Seeing the mark of the nails and putting his hand into Jesus' side
Hearing Jesus say his name, as Mary did at the tomb
Seeing the empty tomb and the folded linen for himself
Eating a meal with Jesus, as the disciples later do by the sea
explanation: "Unless I see in his hands the mark of the nails... I will never believe."

prompt: In John, who is the first person the risen Jesus appears to?
explanation: Mary Magdalene mistakes him for the gardener until he says her name, then tells the disciples she has seen the Lord.

prompt: In John, who asks Pilate for Jesus' body and buries it in a new tomb?
explanation: Joseph of Arimathea, a secret disciple, takes the body, and Nicodemus brings spices for the burial.

prompt: In John, what is the first sign Jesus performs, at a wedding in Cana?
explanation: Jesus turns the water in six stone jars into wine, the first of his signs.

prompt: In John, what does Jesus call himself the day after feeding the five thousand?
explanation: "I am the bread of life; whoever comes to me shall not hunger."

prompt: In John, what does Jesus say he is, so that whoever follows him will not walk in darkness?
explanation: "I am the light of the world. Whoever follows me will not walk in darkness."

prompt: In John, what does Jesus tell Nicodemus a person must be, in order to see the kingdom of God?
explanation: Unless one is born again, or born of water and the Spirit, he cannot see the kingdom of God.

prompt: In John, what does Jesus say happens to a branch that does not abide in him, the true vine?
options: It is thrown away, withers, and is gathered and burned
It is grafted onto a wild olive tree to grow on its own
It bears fruit for one more season before the vinedresser cuts it back
It is left on the vine until the harvest, when the vinedresser sorts it
explanation: Apart from the vine a branch can do nothing; it withers and is thrown into the fire.

prompt: In John, what name does Jesus give the Holy Spirit whom the Father will send in his name?
explanation: The Helper, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in Jesus' name, will teach them all things.

prompt: In John, how many fish do the disciples catch when the risen Jesus tells them to cast the net on the right side of the boat?
explanation: The net is full of 153 large fish, and yet it is not torn.
